actions.reason:
I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py and counted operations by hand. I did not run a new evaluation. All of the estimates below are unmeasured, and every one comes out below the 1% minimum.

Encode: the cost is mostly the Python overhead of each divmod call, not the arithmetic inside it. Dividing by 58**5 instead of 58**4 is still one cheap division per call and would save about 2 calls per 32-byte input. But each group would then need 3 table lookups and 4 small divisions instead of 2 and 2, so the cost per output character rises. A table of three-character entries would have 195112 entries per alphabet, too expensive to build. Merging the last 3 single-group passes into one only saves loop overhead.

Decode: the lane-merge loop takes ceil(log2(length)) steps of 4 big-int operations each. I found no fusion that needs fewer operations. Folding the two cache lookups into one, or reusing one oversized mask table, would save about 500 to 800 instructions per decode. Over the bench's roughly 3000 decodes that is about 0.5 to 0.75% of decode_ir.

Check: earlier rejected attempts showed that swapping the hash function and cleaning up the module header both move check_ir by less than 1%. Its encode and decode paths are the same code as above.

I won't submit a change I expect to miss the minimum.

journal.text:
Test agent here. I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py on the base58-py lineage. I searched for the Python version pins and got 8 matching lines. I counted operations by hand. I made no edits and ran no evaluation.

Nothing was measured. The session ended with no candidate submitted. Every estimate I made came out below the 1% minimum. On encode, the cost sits mostly in the Python overhead of each divmod call, not in the arithmetic. Dividing by 58**5 instead of 58**4 is still one cheap division per call. It saves only a few calls. Not measured yet.

What I believe now is that encode here is already near the floor for pure Python. Shaving divmod calls trims overhead, and the overhead is a small share. The bar stays the same: same bytes out, and a gain above 1%. Hand counts alone do not clear that bar.

Next session I will run lineage_bench.py on the current code first. Then I will profile where encode actually spends its time before I touch anything.
